From 57 Manual Steps to 3 User Actions

Automating multi-client TV advertising alerts — transforming a repetitive, multi-output reporting process into a consolidated Excel workflow with standardized data preparation, summaries, and guided navigation.

The Challenge

Preparing multiple client-specific advertising alerts involved repeated manual work across separate outputs. The process required consistent handling of a shared source dataset, repeated preparation, summary creation, and movement between workbooks.

What made the process demanding

  • Preparing eight distinct alert outputs from a common advertising dataset.
  • Repeating data preparation and selection work for each alert.
  • Maintaining consistency across processed records and summary views.
  • Handling separate workbooks and navigating between report areas.
  • Repeating the same operational sequence each time a new daily file arrived.

The required outcome

A consolidated Excel workbook that provides a common source-data area, eight alert-specific report areas, PivotTable summaries, consistent navigation, and a simple refresh-led operating experience. The goal was to reduce repetitive handling while keeping the outputs organized and easy to review.

The Solution

A unified reporting workbook brings the source, prepared alert data, summaries, and navigation together. The implementation details and alert-specific business rules are intentionally kept confidential.

Centralize

Use one structured source-data area as the common input for the reporting workbook.

Standardize

Apply consistent data-preparation practices before presenting the alert outputs.

Separate outputs

Organize the prepared information into eight distinct alert areas.

Summarize

Provide PivotTable views alongside the prepared report data.

Navigate

Use a Home page and in-sheet navigation to move between report areas.

Refresh

Run the consolidated workflow through a simple user-facing refresh control.

Prepared alert data

Each alert area presents its processed records in a consistent table layout, with navigation to the corresponding summary view.

PivotTable summaries

Summary views sit alongside the reporting workflow, making the prepared information easier to review without switching to a separate workbook.

Measured Results

Three actual daily-file comparisons show a consistent reduction in the time required to prepare the advertising alerts.

Rows in fileManual timeAutomated timeTime reduction
36,20133.21 minutes1.06 minutes96.81%
29,44429.91 minutes55.83 seconds96.89%
27,53227.54 minutes59.16 seconds96.42%

Across the three tests combined, processing time fell by 96.72%, comparing the total recorded manual time with the total automated time. Average manual time was approximately 30.22 minutes; average automated time was approximately 59.53 seconds.

Before

Repeated preparation across multiple alert outputs, separate report handling, and manual movement between workbooks.

After

One consolidated workbook with eight prepared alert areas, summaries, consistent navigation, and a simple refresh-led operating process.

Reporting Design & Confidentiality

The public-facing project page focuses on the business problem, workbook experience, capabilities, and measured results—not on how the automation was implemented.

Designed for practical use

  • One workbook provides access to the source data and all eight alert outputs.
  • Consistent layouts make the report areas easier to understand and review.
  • Branded navigation and clear entry points improve workbook usability.
  • Refresh-led operation reduces repeated manual interaction.

The screenshots and workbook examples shown here use fictionalized names and dummy data. The three performance tests were measured on actual daily files.
